fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Rear-end migration to new turn-lane tapers under changed deceleration expectations is a recognized, scheme-relevant preliminary-design safety issue squarely within FHWA RSA scope.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-016 is cited but with null quote, and the confidence/rationale reveal the rear-end 'pattern' derives from a case-study analog rather than verifiably recorded project data, leaving the central empirical claim weakly anchored.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern/check item with no compliance claim or normative_basis_note, consistent with FHWA RSA prompt-list semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: extend northbound advance warning placement and verify taper storage length against design-year peak queues, both viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Road users limited to vehicle occupants with no acknowledgment of pedestrian interactions introduced by the new auxiliary lane/taper (crossing exposure, channelization), despite marginal VRU relevance.

justifications.substance: Nighttime lighting/retroreflectivity at a pedestrian-bicycle crossing is a substantive preliminary-design-stage safety topic with documented incident history and rising exposure.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Cites EV-US-001 as context and references a single recorded incident, but no quoted content and the rationale admits derivation from case-study patterns rather than scheme-specific evidence.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern distinct from any compliance question, consistent with FHWA RSA guidance where lighting adequacy is raised as a safety issue without normative citation.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and viable at preliminary design (luminaire coverage over the crossing, high-visibility markings), though it omits quantified targets such as illuminance levels or marking specification.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly identified road users and the entire finding centers on their nighttime visibility risk, so VRU impacts are fully considered.
